Management: only under explicit direction (e.g. ACS, mechanical valve), keep INR 2.0-2.5, GI protection with PPI, briefest possible overlap, educate on bleeding signs and never stop either drug on their own.

darunavir (CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition) increases apixaban exposure and bleeding risk. Management: prefer an alternative anticoagulant-dosing plan; avoid strong dual inhibitors outright, halve dose with strong single-pathway inhibition only if physician directed; watch for bleeding signs.

mechanism: darunavir inhibits CYP3A4, raising atorvastatin plasma levels; risk of myopathy and rare rhabdomyolysis is dose-dependent. Management: avoid with simvastatin/lovastatin; for atorvastatin cap at 20 mg/day with strong inhibitors; warn on muscle pain and dark urine, check CK if symptomatic.
source: DDInter 2.0 coverage pattern (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); mechanism/management authored from label-level pharmacology

mechanism: darunavir raises colchicine levels via CYP3A4/P-glycoprotein inhibition; neuromuscular toxicity and bone-marrow suppression reported, lethal in renal impairment. Management: avoid prolonged use together; for gout flares prefer NSAID or steroid; reduce colchicine dose by half and monitor for neuropathy if co-use is unavoidable.
source: DDInter 2.0 coverage pattern (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); mechanism/management authored from label-level pharmacology

mechanism: darunavir inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism of cyclosporine, causing sharp exposure rise with nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity and (tacrolimus) diabetes risk. Management: avoid initiation together; if unavoidable reduce calcineurin-inhibitor dose 50-75%, check trough levels in 2-3 days, monitor creatinine and potassium.
source: DDInter 2.0 coverage pattern (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); mechanism/management authored from label-level pharmacology

mechanism: erythromycin (CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition) increases apixaban exposure and bleeding risk. Management: prefer an alternative anticoagulant-dosing plan; avoid strong dual inhibitors outright, halve dose with strong single-pathway inhibition only if physician directed; watch for bleeding signs.
source: DDInter 2.0 coverage pattern (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); mechanism/management authored from label-level pharmacology

mechanism: erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4, raising atorvastatin plasma levels; risk of myopathy and rare rhabdomyolysis is dose-dependent. Management: avoid with simvastatin/lovastatin; for atorvastatin cap at 20 mg/day with strong inhibitors; warn on muscle pain and dark urine, check CK if symptomatic.
source: DDInter 2.0 coverage pattern (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); mechanism/management authored from label-level pharmacology

mechanism: erythromycin raises colchicine levels via CYP3A4/P-glycoprotein inhibition; neuromuscular toxicity and bone-marrow suppression reported, lethal in renal impairment. Management: avoid prolonged use together; for gout flares prefer NSAID or steroid; reduce colchicine dose by half and monitor for neuropathy if co-use is unavoidable.
source: DDInter 2.0 coverage pattern (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); mechanism/management authored from label-level pharmacology

mechanism: erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism of cyclosporine, causing sharp exposure rise with nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity and (tacrolimus) diabetes risk. Management: avoid initiation together; if unavoidable reduce calcineurin-inhibitor dose 50-75%, check trough levels in 2-3 days, monitor creatinine and potassium.
source: DDInter 2.0 coverage pattern (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); mechanism/management authored from label-level pharmacology

mechanism: erythromycin increases domperidone levels through CYP3A4 inhibition (QT/haematologic/toxicity concerns). Management: reduce the lower-risk drug dose where feasible, ECG if QT-relevant, monitor CBC for imatinib; avoid domperidone with strong inhibitors.
source: DDInter 2.0 coverage pattern (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); mechanism/management authored from label-level pharmacology

mechanism: erythromycin slows theophylline clearance; nausea and tachyarrhythmia risk. Management: monitor level or reduce dose ~30% during the antibiotic course.

Management: baseline ECG with QTc before co-prescription, correct potassium/magnesium, prefer non-QT alternatives; avoid in known long-QT syndrome.

mechanism: voriconazole slows CYP3A4 clearance of sildenafil, potentiating vasodilation, headache and hypotension. Management: start at the lowest PDE5 dose, avoid re-dosing, advise on symptomatic hypotension.

mechanism: voriconazole inhibits CYP3A4, raising simvastatin plasma levels; risk of myopathy and rare rhabdomyolysis is dose-dependent. Management: avoid with simvastatin/lovastatin; for atorvastatin cap at 20 mg/day with strong inhibitors; warn on muscle pain and dark urine, check CK if symptomatic.
source: DDInter 2.0 coverage pattern (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0); mechanism/management authored from label-level pharmacology

mechanism: voriconazole inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism of tacrolimus, causing sharp exposure rise with nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity and (tacrolimus) diabetes risk. Management: avoid initiation together; if unavoidable reduce calcineurin-inhibitor dose 50-75%, check trough levels in 2-3 days, monitor creatinine and potassium.
